data.gender_notes: Swaroopam is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: An embodiment of eternal beauty and divinity. The name Swaroopam carries the meaning “Eternal Image or Form” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Swaroopam usually hope their child will grow to embody eternal image or form and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine form or image.
data.etymology: Swaroopam belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Eternal Image or Form.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Swaroopam total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Swaroopam holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism. The Sanskrit word Swaroopam is derived from Swaroop, meaning form or appearance. It implies an embodiment of eternal beauty and grace, a personification of the divine. In Indian art, mythology, and culture, deities and gods are often depicted in their Swaroop, or divine forms, showcasing their magnificent appearance and divine powers.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper spiritual level, the name Swaroopam represents the divine form or inner Self of an individual, connecting them to the Source of all creation. It is a reminder that we are all divine beings, bearing the celestial qualities of the universe within us. Swaroopam signifies the manifestation of that divinity in our daily lives, encouraging us to seek inner beauty, strength, and wisdom.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Swaroopam signifies the divine form or the inner self, which is inherently divine and eternal, beyond the limitations of the physical body and worldly identities. It is a reminder of the ultimate reality of being, where the individual soul merges back into the infinite cosmic consciousness.

historical_references.reference: Swaroopam was the name of a powerful Jain monk who lived during the 12th and 13th centuries. He was a disciple of the Jain poet-philosopher Hemachandra. Swaroopam is known for his teachings on Jainism, particularly his commentary on the Yoga-Sutras of Patanjali.

Swaroopam is also the name of a 16th-century Hindu king who ruled the Vijayanagara Empire. He is known for his military conquests and his patronage of art and architecture. The most notable example of his architectural patronage is the Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple in Srirangam.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Swaroopam' holds deep spiritual significance in Hinduism, meaning 'Form of the Divine'. In today's world, this name is not only used symbolically but also as a personal branding statement across various platforms. On LinkedIn, individuals may use it as a professional handle to represent their unique identity and expertise. On Instagram, it can be seen as a hashtag for spiritual growth and self-expression, where individuals share inspiring quotes, practices, and experiences related to their inner journey. On Medium, Swaroopam can be used as a pen name for authors writing about personal development, mindfulness, and the pursuit of the divine within.
